notes.note: Re-reviewed Release updates against desktop_update.rs at this revision: restore now runs at the start of the periodic thread (state idle meanwhile), needs a version-bound signature (plugin restore_update sets require_signed_version), and is followed by one feed check that drops a withdrawn or superseded package and keeps it when the feed does not answer; a damaged package at install returns to idle with an install error. The text states macOS archives carry the version only from the #3851 signing change, so earlier macOS packages are discarded at the next start.

Added the version-binding rule: tauri-updater-manifest.mjs refuses an unversioned or mismatched signature when assembling latest.json, and macos-notarized-artifacts signs with --app-version from CFBundleShortVersionString (both workflows assert it equals the manifest version). The windows-nightly test only gained versioned signature fixtures.

Added that each cohort signature must name the cohort version; checked against createUpdaterManifestForPlatforms, which windows-nightly.mjs and the nightly CLI step both use. The macOS signer change is the --app-version flag; the rest of the macOS flow described here is unchanged.
windows-nightly.test.ts only replaced fake signature strings with version-bound ones; no claim here concerns signature contents.
native-platform-boundary.mjs now lexes JSON5/TOML past comments and escapes and reads Tauri configs only at app.security.capabilities; the document's least-privilege claims still hold.
